overview: The Greek city-states formed a varied political and cultural world. These examples focus on Athens and Classical sculpture; Athenian institutions should not be assumed to describe every Greek community.

items.text: Athenian potters controlled the air admitted to a kiln in successive firing stages to produce contrasting black and red surfaces.
Red-figure vase painting developed around 530 BCE. Brush-drawn details gave painters greater freedom to show anatomy, fabric and movement.
Polykleitos developed a system of bodily proportions. Many renowned Greek bronze compositions are known through later marble copies and written descriptions.
The marble Parthenon belonged to the building program associated with Perikles and the worship of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis.
In Classical Athens, adult male citizens participated in the assembly. This was a particular civic institution, not political participation for every resident.
Different vessel shapes served storage, water carrying, drinking and ritual. Pottery images complement written evidence about Athenian life.
